caption:
Google AI Overviews are moving the link to your website lower. Small business checklist: 4 things to put on your site so Google's AI answers still link to you.

On November 24, Search Engine Roundtable shared new data from Peec AI, a company that tracks AI search. On September 21, 76.8% of Google's AI Overviews showed their first link in the top third of the answer. By November 20, that was 51.8%.

The same day, Google published a guide on how AI Overviews and AI Mode pick the pages they link to. Google says its AI links to the pages that support the information in the answer, and it asks site owners to keep important information in text and give clear background on who they are.

Here's what we'd put in place first:
1. Your hours, prices and services written as plain text on your site, not only inside images.
2. An About page that says who you are, where you are and what you do.
3. One clear page for each service you sell.
4. The same facts everywhere: your site, your Google Business Profile and your Instagram.

Google AI Overviews now show the first link to a website lower in the answer, and that matters for every small business that gets found on Google.

Search Engine Roundtable reported on November 24 that, according to Peec AI data, the share of AI Overviews with their first link in the top third of the answer fell from 76.8% on September 21 to 51.8% on November 20.

caption_drafts.provocation:
If Google's AI answer already gives a customer your hours, why would they click through to your small business website?

That question got sharper this week. On November 24, Search Engine Roundtable shared Peec AI data showing the first link in Google AI Overviews now lands in the top third of the answer only 51.8% of the time, down from 76.8% in September.

Google says its AI links the pages that back up its answer. A site with clear facts in plain text gives it a reason to link to you. A site where your prices live inside a flyer image gives it very little.
